description: The accounting program helps students prepare for a variety of careers in accounting, finance and business, including positions as CPAs, auditors, tax accountants, financial analysts and forensic accountants. The Bachelor of Science degree in accounting prepares students to pursue certification as a CPA in Texas or in other states that require 150 hours of college credit. The program satisfies the undergraduate requirements for admission to the Master of Science degree in accounting or the MBA with a concentration in accounting. The BS in accounting provides a broad understanding of accounting issues for those who plan to pursue careers in accounting and business. In addition, the program serves as a strong foundation for students who plan to pursue graduate studies in accounting, business, or law. The program is accredited by AACSB International.

The Bachelor of Science/Master of Science in accounting (BS/MS) program is designed for students seeking to qualify for the Uniform CPA Examination while simultaneously earning both a bachelor’s degree and a master’s degree in a focused and efficient timeframe. The BS/MS accounting program offers high-ability students the opportunity to earn both degrees in as little as five years. Students applying for the BS/MS accounting program must select a graduate major: Accounting, MS, or Taxation, MS. For specific requirements for these programs, please refer to the College of Business, Department of Accounting, website. Admission to the BS/MS program is competitive and requires a separate application from the general university admission process.

The minor in acoustics is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a basic understanding of acoustical principles. The minor is offered by the College of Engineering and the College of Music in collaboration with the Department of Physics. Students completing this minor will gain knowledge in the measurement, analysis, and perception of sound, and will be prepared to apply this knowledge to a wide variety of careers including architectural acoustics, audio engineering, environmental noise, and biomedical acoustics.

Addiction is one of society's most complex and challenging problems. It is an epidemic that impacts individuals, families, communities, and nations. The University of North Texas has developed a comprehensive Bachelor of Science degree in Addiction Studies to prepare students to be leaders in the addiction profession. This program provides a strong foundation in addiction theory, prevention, treatment, and recovery. Students will learn about the biological, psychological, sociological, and spiritual aspects of addiction, as well as the legal and ethical considerations of working with individuals and families affected by addiction. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practices, cultural competence, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Upon completion of the program, students will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the addiction field, including addiction counselor, prevention specialist, case manager, and recovery coach. The program also provides a solid foundation for graduate studies in addiction, counseling, social work, and related fields.

The Addiction Studies minor, housed in the Department of Rehabilitation and Health Services, provides students with an understanding of addictive behaviors. The minor is designed to serve students interested in working in the addiction field. The curriculum provides core competencies required for certification as an LCDC (Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor) in Texas. Students are responsible for verifying specific certification requirements with the Texas Health and Human Services Commission.

The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in advertising emphasizes creativity and problem-solving skills in developing advertising messages for a variety of media. Students learn strategic planning, media placement and research in preparation for careers as advertising professionals. Advertising faculty members have extensive professional experience and actively engage students in creative work and research. Many students gain professional experience through internships at advertising agencies or with corporate marketing departments. The major prepares students for careers in media planning, account management, creative services, production, research and other areas in advertising.

The Aerospace Studies minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of aerospace power and its role in national security. Students will learn about the history of air power, the development of military aviation, and the organization and operations of the United States Air Force and Space Force. The minor complements a wide range of academic majors, offering a unique perspective on leadership, global affairs, and technological advancement within the aerospace domain. It also serves as an excellent foundation for students considering a commission in the U.S. Air Force or U.S. Space Force through the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC) program, though enrollment in AFROTC is not required to pursue the minor.

The Africana Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a systematic and critical understanding of the experiences of African peoples in the United States, Africa, and the Caribbean. Drawing primarily upon the insights and methods of the social sciences and humanities, the curriculum focuses on topics such as the history of African peoples, socio-economic and political developments, cultural forms, and gender issues. The minor provides an excellent foundation for students interested in careers in teaching, government, law, social work, business, journalism, or public policy. It is also an excellent option for students planning to pursue graduate studies in Africana studies or related fields.

The American Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a broad understanding of American culture through a wide variety of courses in the humanities, social sciences and fine arts. The minor helps students develop critical and analytical skills that prepare them for a variety of careers in fields such as business, education, government, journalism, law, public administration, and social work. The minor in American Studies offers a strong background for graduate study in American Studies, history, literature, and other fields.

The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in anthropology requires a minimum of 120 credit hours, 42 of which must be advanced, and fulfillment of the university's core curriculum requirements. The degree program is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the four fields of anthropology: archaeology, cultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology and physical anthropology.

The Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences (BAAS) is an interdisciplinary degree designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Arts and Sciences (AAAS), Associate of Applied Science (AAS) or other applied associate’s degree and desire to complete a bachelor’s degree. The degree provides an opportunity for career and technical education courses to apply toward a bachelor’s degree program. Students must complete 36 hours of upper-division courses, of which 18 hours must be in one of the following specializations or 18 hours of upper-division courses approved by an advisor if no specialization is chosen or available. The remaining 18 hours of upper-division courses may be chosen from other specializations offered through the BAAS program or from other approved upper-division course work in order to complete the 36 hours.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) provides students with a strong academic background, including conceptual knowledge of behavior analysis and practical skills for working in areas requiring the application of behavior analytic principles. Applied behavior analysis is the scientific study of human behavior with a focus on understanding why people do what they do and how to help people acquire new skills and change behavior. The curriculum is designed to provide coursework needed for students to become a Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst® (BCaBA®), an undergraduate-level certification provided by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB®). Students graduating with this degree will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the field, including those working with individuals with autism spectrum disorder and related disabilities, traumatic brain injury, organizational behavior management, and behavioral medicine. The program prepares students for graduate study in behavior analysis or other related fields.

The Applied Gerontology minor provides students with a broad knowledge base regarding the process of aging and older adults. Students gain an understanding of the physiological, psychological, and sociological aspects of aging, and learn about policy, services, and programs for older adults. This minor is an excellent complement to many majors across the university (e.g., health studies, psychology, sociology, hospitality, recreation, business, public health, nursing, nutrition, social work).

The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Art Education is a professional degree providing a strong studio-based curriculum with a focus on preparing highly qualified art teachers for all levels of public and private schools. This degree combines professional education and studio art to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to become successful art educators. Art education majors will develop their artistic voice through study in a broad range of studio disciplines including drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, new media, and ceramics. The Art Education program is designed to fulfill the requirements for the Texas All-Level (EC-12) Art Teacher Certification.

Concentration name: Art Museum Education, Fashion History, Pre-Art Conservation
description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Art History provides students with a broad and deep education in art and its history. The program prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, cultural institutions, and education, or for advanced studies in art history, museum studies, or related fields. Students develop critical thinking, visual analysis, research, and writing skills as they explore art from diverse cultures and periods.

This minor is designed to supplement other majors. The student who majors in art studio, communication design or visual art studies will find the minor in art history gives breadth to a course of study and prepares the student for graduate work in art history. Students who major in other areas will find the minor in art history a useful and enlightening complement to other majors.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Artificial Intelligence prepares students for careers in the rapidly growing field of AI, including machine learning, deep learning, data science, robotics, computer vision, natural language processing, and other emerging AI areas. This program offers a comprehensive curriculum covering the theoretical foundations, algorithms, and practical applications of AI. It emphasizes hands-on experience through projects and laboratory work, equipping students with the skills to design, develop, and deploy intelligent systems. Graduates will be prepared for various roles in industry, government, and research, as well as for further graduate studies in AI and related fields.

This major prepares students for graduate study and careers in audiology and speech-language pathology by providing a strong science-based foundation. Graduate study is required for certification and licensure as an audiologist or speech-language pathologist. The faculty are committed to providing students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue a graduate degree and to succeed as professionals. The curriculum combines basic science courses with general education and core courses in communication disorders. Students who successfully complete the undergraduate program are prepared to enter graduate programs in audiology (Au.D.) and speech-language pathology (M.S.).

The Aviation Logistics program at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare students for management and operational careers in the aviation industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in aviation, business, and logistics principles, focusing on the unique challenges and opportunities within the aerospace sector. Students will gain expertise in areas such as airline operations, airport management, supply chain logistics, regulatory compliance, safety management, and aviation finance. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and leadership skills, equipping graduates to effectively manage resources, optimize operations, and contribute to the efficiency and sustainability of aviation organizations. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, hands-on projects, and opportunities for internships, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the global aviation industry and be prepared for diverse roles in airlines, airports, MROs (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul facilities), aerospace manufacturing, and governmental agencies.

Biochemistry is the study of the chemical and physical processes that occur within living organisms. It is a fundamental discipline that is at the heart of the biological sciences. The interdisciplinary nature of biochemistry means that students are well prepared for careers in fields such as health care, forensics, environmental science, and pharmaceutical research and development. The Biochemistry BA program provides a solid foundation for further study in graduate or professional school. The Biochemistry program is designed to provide students with a strong background in the molecular sciences and quantitative skills. The curriculum includes courses in general and organic chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, and biochemistry. Through laboratory experiences, students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills that are essential for success in a wide range of careers.

The biochemistry program offers students the opportunity to learn about the chemical processes occurring in living systems. Biochemistry is a central science that bridges biology and chemistry. Understanding biochemistry is critical to making advances in fields such as medicine, biotechnology, agriculture and environmental science. In addition to gaining a fundamental understanding of life processes, the biochemistry major prepares students for graduate study in biochemistry, chemistry or cell/molecular biology, or for professional schools such as medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine. It also provides an excellent foundation for immediate employment in biotechnology, pharmacology, environmental science or laboratory research.

The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Biology is a liberal arts degree primarily intended for students preparing for careers in the health professions, secondary teaching, environmental sciences, or business. This program emphasizes a broad background in biology with supporting work in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Students may apply for admission to graduate programs in various areas of biology and the health sciences.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Biology is designed for students who desire a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics. The curriculum provides the necessary breadth of knowledge and training in the major areas of biology to prepare students for successful entry into graduate school, medical and other health-related professional programs, or science-related careers. All students are advised to meet with an academic advisor in the Department of Biological Sciences each semester. A comprehensive listing of all requirements can be found in the current University of North Texas Undergraduate Catalog and by consulting with an academic advisor.
The minor in biology requires a minimum of 18 hours in biology, of which 6 hours must be advanced (3000- or 4000-level).

Biomedical Engineering combines fundamental engineering principles with biology and medicine to create new knowledge and technology to improve health outcomes and quality of life. Biomedical Engineers apply engineering concepts and methods to solve problems in biology and medicine. This can include the design of medical instruments, artificial organs, prostheses, and systems that deliver health care. The biomedical engineering curriculum provides students with a strong background in engineering science and design, mathematics, and physical and biological sciences and provides the necessary foundation for a career as a practicing biomedical engineer or for graduate studies in engineering, medicine, or other health sciences.
Accreditation status: The Biomedical Engineering Program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

description: The British and Irish Studies minor provides students with the opportunity to examine the interdisciplinary aspects of British and Irish culture. The minor examines the rich traditions and enduring impact of two of the world’s most influential cultures. The program is designed for students seeking to complement their major with studies in British and Irish history, literature, politics, and culture.

Business analytics is the practice of iterative, methodical exploration of an organization’s data, with an emphasis on statistical analysis, to drive decision-making. Business analytics is used to gain insights that inform business decisions. Analytics tools and techniques are used to explore data, understand past performance, and predict future outcomes. The BBA in Business Analytics prepares students to work in any industry to improve business performance using data-driven insights. Students learn how to collect, manage and analyze data and interpret the results to provide decision makers with the insights needed to improve business processes and grow revenue.
Accreditation status: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

description: The Minor in Business Computer Information Systems provides students with foundational knowledge in information systems relevant to business operations. Students will gain an understanding of database management, systems analysis and design, and business programming concepts, preparing them for roles where technology intersects with business strategy. This minor complements a wide range of majors by enhancing students' analytical and technical skills in an increasingly data-driven world.
A minor in business is offered to students in non-business majors. Students interested in this minor should contact the office of the G. Brint Ryan College of Business for advising information.

The minor in Business/Public Administration is designed for non-business majors interested in acquiring some general business knowledge. This minor requires 18 hours of course work in general business topics that are beneficial in almost any career.

The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in chemistry is a more flexible degree program requiring fewer total chemistry hours than the Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in chemistry. The BA degree is recommended for students preparing for careers such as those in the health professions (pre-medicine, pre-dentistry, etc.), patent law, business, science writing or secondary science teaching. Graduate study in chemistry would require taking more than the minimum number of chemistry courses required for the BA degree. Students planning graduate work in chemistry should consult with a chemistry advisor or consider the BS in chemistry degree.

The Department of Chemistry offers an undergraduate program leading to the Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science degrees. Both are designed to provide students with a strong background in chemistry, either as a terminal degree or as preparation for further professional or graduate study. Students seeking a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry can be certified to the American Chemical Society (ACS) by completing 15 hours of courses beyond the basic chemistry curriculum.
Accreditation status: American Chemical Society (ACS) Approved, with certification option upon completion of specific coursework.

description: The minor in chemistry is designed primarily for students in biology and related health professions. The minor is also appropriate for students who wish to supplement their major with a strong background in chemistry.

The Minor in Child Development and Family Studies requires 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). At least 9 hours must be taken at UNT. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor. For more information regarding a specific course, please consult the UNT undergraduate catalog. Required courses: CDFS 2310, CDFS 2340, CDFS 3313, CDFS 3360, CDFS 4333. One advanced CDFS elective (3000/4000 level).

The minor in Classical Studies provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the world of the Greeks and Romans and its legacy. Students choose from a range of courses in history, art history, philosophy, and classical languages. The minor allows students to apply classical perspectives to their own lives and the modern world.

Communication Design students learn to develop strategic visual solutions across various media, including print, screen, and emerging technologies. Graduates are prepared for professional practice in fields such as graphic design, interaction design, web design, app design, information architecture, user experience design, and motion graphics. Communication Design is a professional program within the College of Visual Arts and Design. Students learn design principles, theories, and processes applied to visual communication. The program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and creative execution relevant to contemporary design practices. Students select either a Graphic Design or an Interaction Design concentration.

The Communication Studies program gives students opportunities to understand the communication process, to improve their communication abilities, and to apply those skills in a variety of contexts. It emphasizes the development of critical thinking, problem solving, listening, speaking, reading and writing skills. Because Communication Studies is a versatile degree, students are able to pursue a variety of careers in fields such as business and industry, government, law, education, health and social services, media, and the arts. Students acquire a strong theoretical and practical knowledge of the communication discipline. Emphasis is on acquiring effective communication skills in interpersonal, group, organizational, public and intercultural settings. The program helps students develop skills in analyzing, designing and evaluating messages.

A minor in Communication Studies provides students with a broad understanding of the role of communication in society and in human interaction. Course work in the minor focuses on communication theory, research and processes, and develops students’ abilities to think critically about communication problems, messages and effects.

Computer engineering is a discipline that bridges electrical engineering and computer science, combining hardware and software aspects. Computer engineers design and develop computer systems and other technological devices. The computer engineering curriculum includes topics such as computer organization and architecture, microprocessors, digital logic design, computer networks, and embedded systems. With a degree in computer engineering, students can pursue careers in areas such as computer hardware design, embedded systems development, network engineering, and cybersecurity.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science degree program in Computer Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science requires 120 credit hours for the degree. It has a strong math and science component and requires a minor outside the department. This degree is designed to prepare students for careers in applications programming, database administration, information technology, web development, research and development, and advanced studies in computer science. Graduates may work in government, education, business or industry.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Computer Science is designed to prepare students for a career in software development and related areas or for graduate study in computer science. Students in the program receive a solid foundation in both the theoretical and applied aspects of computer science. The curriculum includes courses in programming languages, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering. Technical electives allow students to specialize in areas such as artificial intelligence, computer graphics, computer networks, cyber security, database systems, and mobile application development. The BS program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.

description: A minor in computer science offers the opportunity to acquire basic understanding of problem-solving techniques using the computer. A knowledge of computer science is invaluable in today's job market, regardless of the major.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Construction Engineering Technology (CET) provides the knowledge and skills for managing the construction process. The curriculum emphasizes the application of scientific and engineering principles to the construction of civil, residential, industrial, and commercial facilities. The program provides the graduate with the technical and managerial skills for careers in construction project management, field supervision, estimating, scheduling, quality control, materials testing and inspection, and safety. The program requires 120 credit hours.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Construction Management (CM) prepares students for professional careers in the construction industry. Construction is the nation’s largest single industry and professionals working in CM apply business, scientific, engineering, and technology principles to solve the challenges associated with the delivery of complex construction projects. The CM program at UNT is a business-centric program housed in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business that focuses on the business, management, and technology of construction. Graduates will be able to contribute to project delivery immediately upon graduation.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Consumer Experience Management (CEM) focuses on the strategies and skills necessary to create positive consumer experiences in a dynamic, global, customer-centric environment. The CEM program integrates experiential learning opportunities that prepare graduates to meet the needs of diverse consumers throughout the consumer journey. The curriculum helps students develop critical and creative thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, and competencies in professional communication and teamwork. Graduates are prepared for careers that involve understanding, engaging and managing consumer experiences across various industries including retail, services, hospitality, tourism, nonprofit, and healthcare. Graduates will find jobs in organizations in areas such as consumer experience management, market research, brand management, data analysis, business development, and customer relationship management.

The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in Converged Broadcast Media is offered by the Department of Media Arts. The curriculum is designed to produce graduates capable of creating professional audio, video and interactive media for broadcast, streaming and online distribution. It prepares students for careers in the dynamic media production and distribution fields, including positions as producers, directors, writers, editors, photojournalists, talent, content creators, and marketing/promotions professionals.

The bachelor of science degree in criminal justice provides students with an understanding of the causes of crime, the nature of offenders and victims, and the various components of the criminal justice system. The program provides the knowledge and skills necessary for effective and efficient performance in the criminal justice system and in related occupations. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to the field of criminal justice and to develop their analytical and critical thinking skills. It also serves as a foundation for graduate study in criminal justice and related disciplines.

The minor in criminal justice is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in criminal justice or a related field, but whose major is in another area of study. The minor provides students with a foundational understanding of the criminal justice system, including law enforcement, courts, and corrections, as well as an introduction to criminal behavior and relevant social science theories. Students will develop critical thinking skills and an understanding of ethical issues in criminal justice. The minor is flexible and can be tailored to meet the individual interests of students.

The Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the theoretical and practical aspects of cybersecurity. Cybersecurity is a critical field focused on protecting computer systems, networks, and data from digital attacks and unauthorized access. This program equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand, identify, and mitigate cybersecurity threats, ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of information. Students will gain expertise in areas such as network security, secure software development, cryptography, digital forensics, ethical hacking, risk management, and compliance. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience, problem-solving, and critical thinking, preparing graduates for a wide range of careers in both the public and private sectors, including roles as cybersecurity analysts, security engineers, incident responders, and forensic specialists. The program is committed to producing highly skilled cybersecurity professionals capable of addressing the complex challenges of the evolving cyber landscape.

The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Dance prepares students to be critically engaged artists, articulate communicators, and thoughtful citizens, who understand the role of dance in society, and whose knowledge and experience are firmly rooted in diverse approaches to contemporary dance practices. Students develop their creative voice through choreographic research, performance, dance scholarship, and pedagogical practices grounded in equity, diversity, and inclusion. This comprehensive program encourages collaboration across disciplines, engagement in community initiatives, and the pursuit of individual passions. The BA in Dance curriculum serves as a foundation for multiple career pathways within the field of dance, including professional performance, choreography, pedagogy, community engagement, arts administration, somatic practices, and graduate studies.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance is a rigorous, pre-professional degree designed to develop the dance artist. The curriculum includes advanced study in various dance techniques, choreography, dance history, movement analysis, somatic practices, and performance. The goal of the program is to prepare students for professional careers in dance performance, choreography, teaching, or further graduate study. Students will engage in intensive studio work, theoretical studies, and performance opportunities, fostering critical thinking, creativity, and a comprehensive understanding of the art of dance.

The minor in Dance requires 18 hours, including 6 hours of Dance major technique courses (DANC 1515, 1516, 2515, 2516, 3515, 3516, 4515, 4516) at the 2000 level or above. Students must be able to place into at least DANC 2515 or 2516. Only students who have demonstrated dance technique ability through audition and placement during the first week of classes are eligible to enroll in these courses. Only courses with a grade of C or better count toward the minor. No more than 6 hours of upper-division courses from other departments may be applied toward the minor. For more information, contact the Department of Dance.

The minor in Data Analytics introduces students to fundamental concepts and techniques in data analytics. Students gain an understanding of how data are used to support decision-making and how to apply quantitative methods and computational tools to analyze data. The minor offers practical skills in data management, statistical analysis, predictive modeling, and data visualization. Students learn to interpret data insights and communicate findings effectively, preparing them for careers in various fields where data-driven decisions are crucial. This minor can complement a wide range of majors by providing essential data literacy and analytical capabilities relevant in today’s data-intensive world.

The Bachelor of Science in Data Science is an interdisciplinary degree that provides students with strong statistical, mathematical and computational skills that are essential for analyzing and interpreting complex data sets. Students will gain experience with modern machine learning and statistical modeling tools and software, database management, and programming skills that allow them to integrate all aspects of the data science pipeline. A degree in Data Science prepares students for careers in fields ranging from health care, engineering, and government to finance, insurance and social media, among many others. In addition, the degree provides students with a strong foundation for graduate studies in data science or related fields.

The Digital and Print Journalism, BA program prepares students for careers in news and information industries across a wide array of formats and platforms. The curriculum emphasizes the fundamental values of journalism—truth, accuracy, fairness and independence—while teaching skills essential for success in today’s rapidly evolving media landscape. Students learn to report, write, edit, design and produce content using cutting-edge digital tools for newspapers, magazines, websites, mobile platforms, radio, television and other media. The program also provides a strong foundation in media law and ethics, critical thinking, visual communication and entrepreneurship, preparing graduates to adapt to new technologies and take on leadership roles in the field. Graduates find careers as reporters, editors, producers, content creators, social media managers, public relations specialists, fact-checkers and media entrepreneurs.

Digital retailing refers to the application of digital technology, processes and business models to enhance, improve and create value for the customer experience. Digital retailing requires the integration of technology and strategy within the retailing context to improve the shopping experience of consumers and achieve competitive advantage for retailers. The Bachelor of Science degree in Digital Retailing is designed to educate students about the strategies and processes related to successfully leveraging digital innovations within a retailing context. The program includes hands-on experience with technologies such as web analytics, mobile payment systems, digital signage, social media applications, augmented/virtual reality, and much more. Students graduating with a Digital Retailing BS degree will be well prepared to pursue careers in digital marketing, social media marketing, digital merchandising, e-commerce, mobile retailing, user experience, visual merchandising, analytics, strategy and technology. The program also helps students prepare for graduate school.

The Bachelor of Arts with a major in economics is designed for students seeking a liberal arts education that combines economics with a breadth of courses from other academic disciplines. This degree is especially valuable for students interested in careers in government, law, international affairs, journalism and liberal arts. Students are required to demonstrate foreign language proficiency.

The undergraduate program in economics is designed to acquaint students with the basic analytical tools and factual information necessary for understanding contemporary economic problems and policies. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in economic theory, quantitative methods and applied economics. An understanding of economic principles is valuable not only for students pursuing careers as economists in government or business, but also for those seeking careers in law, public administration, finance, business administration and other fields where decision making and policy formulation play a prominent role. The department offers a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in economics and a Bachelor of Science (BS) with a major in economics. The BBA degree provides students with a broad background in business with a major in economics. The BS degree provides a strong analytical background and is more quantitative in nature. The department also offers an Economics minor.

The minor in economics is designed for students who desire to supplement a major in another field with additional work in economics. It provides a useful background for those students whose career objectives include business or other areas where economic analysis is important. It also provides a useful foundation for graduate work in economics.

Electrical engineers work in many fields, including energy, communications, computers, controls, microelectronics and manufacturing. The undergraduate curriculum provides a broad background in topics essential to the discipline of electrical engineering through a required core of courses, with opportunities to specialize through electives. The electrical engineering program prepares students to enter a diverse global workforce and succeed in graduate studies or professional careers. Graduates are able to identify and solve engineering problems, demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility, communicate effectively, apply advanced mathematics and science to engineering problems, and work effectively on multi-disciplinary teams.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: This minor provides students with a foundational understanding of emergency administration and planning. It is designed for students interested in careers in emergency management, disaster preparedness, response, recovery, or related fields. The minor emphasizes practical applications, critical thinking, and interdisciplinary approaches to addressing complex challenges posed by emergencies and disasters. Students will gain knowledge and skills in risk assessment, mitigation, preparedness planning, incident management, and recovery strategies, preparing them to contribute effectively to resilient communities.

The Engineering Management, BS program prepares students for leadership positions that require both technical and managerial skills. This interdisciplinary degree blends engineering fundamentals with business and management principles to equip graduates with the knowledge to manage projects, teams and operations in technology-driven organizations. Students learn to optimize processes, improve efficiency, manage resources and make strategic decisions in complex engineering environments. The curriculum includes courses in engineering science, mathematics, statistics, economics, accounting, finance, marketing, organizational behavior, operations management and project management.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering Management program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Writing and Rhetoric; Language and Literature; Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12
description: The English department at UNT offers an undergraduate curriculum designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the English language and its literature. Students majoring in English may choose from three areas of concentration: Writing and Rhetoric; Language and Literature; and Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12. Students concentrating in Writing and Rhetoric study the theoretical and practical dimensions of writing in various contexts. They will develop their analytical, critical, and interpretive skills, preparing them for graduate work in rhetoric, professional writing, and related fields, as well as for careers in technical and business writing, editing, publishing, law, and government. Students concentrating in Language and Literature study language, literary history and traditions, and literary theory. They will prepare for graduate study in literature and related fields, and for careers in editing, publishing, and other professions demanding strong analytical, critical, interpretive, and communication skills. Students concentrating in Teacher Certification in English, Language Arts, and Reading, Grades 7–12, study English language arts content and the theory and practice of teaching. They prepare for careers as secondary school teachers.

The Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Management minor provides students with the business and management skills necessary to launch a new venture or work for a rapidly growing existing venture. Students learn how to identify, evaluate and exploit entrepreneurial opportunities; develop business plans; acquire resources; commercialize technology; and manage fast-growing organizations. The minor is available to all non-business majors, and to business majors who are not pursuing a major in Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Management. The minor may be pursued as part of the undergraduate degree by approval of the student's major department and the G. Brint Ryan College of Business.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science prepares students for a diverse array of careers. Graduates are qualified for positions in government agencies, private industry and environmental consulting firms. In addition, the program provides an excellent background for students who wish to pursue graduate degrees in Environmental Science, Water Resource Science and Management, or related fields. The program is designed to provide students with a strong background in science, mathematics, statistics and computer science, as well as an understanding of environmental policy and regulations. Students completing the degree will be well prepared to address current and future environmental issues.

The Event Design and Experience Management (EDEM) program prepares students to become leaders in the fast-growing and dynamic global events industry. Students will learn the process of designing, planning, marketing, operating, and evaluating various types of events, including corporate events, festivals, concerts, conferences, and sports events. The curriculum emphasizes creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and sustainable practices relevant to the event industry. Graduates will be equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to create memorable and impactful experiences for diverse audiences.
Program name: Event Design and Experience Management, BS

description: Students interested in a career in the fashion industry will find a dynamic and creative learning environment in the Fashion Design BFA program. The program prepares students for professional careers in the design of apparel, accessories, textiles and related fields, or for further graduate study. Students develop knowledge and skills in design, aesthetic judgment, merchandising, sourcing, and marketing. Graduates are employed in a variety of design and creative positions including apparel designers, product developers, technical designers, patternmakers, illustrators, textile designers and merchandisers for manufacturers and retailers, or they may choose to pursue graduate studies.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Fibers provides an in-depth curriculum of studio practice with supporting art history and critical studies course work. The program emphasizes an understanding of traditional and experimental media and processes in contemporary art. Students are introduced to a wide range of materials and techniques with opportunity for in-depth study in areas such as weaving, dyeing, surface design, non-woven fiber construction, digital textile design, and other interdisciplinary approaches. Graduates are prepared for careers as professional artists, studio assistants, designers, art educators, and for graduate study.

The Bachelor of Arts in Film, Television and Digital Media is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the historical, theoretical, critical and aesthetic dimensions of the moving image. Through a combination of coursework, hands-on production experiences, and critical analysis, students develop skills in storytelling, media analysis, production techniques, and ethical considerations within the evolving media landscape. The program prepares students for careers in the film, television, and digital media industries, as well as for advanced studies in media arts.
Program name: Film, Television and Digital Media, BA

description: The Bachelor of Business Administration, major in Finance, emphasizes the financial aspects of managerial decisions. This program prepares students for positions in corporate finance, investment management, banking, insurance and real estate. The curriculum provides an understanding of how managers and investors can best make decisions in financial markets given different risk and return tradeoffs.

The Department of Finance offers a minor in finance for non-business majors. The minor provides an understanding of financial decision-making for managing individuals' and organizations' financial assets and liabilities, and the functioning of financial markets. It helps prepare students for careers in banking, real estate, personal financial planning, corporate finance, and the financial services industry generally.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Financial Planning prepares students for successful careers in financial planning and provides the academic background necessary to sit for the Certified Financial Planner (CFP®) examination. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in personal financial planning, investment, risk management and insurance, employee benefits and retirement planning, estate planning and income tax planning. The financial planning curriculum provides the academic background necessary for students to pursue graduate studies in financial planning, law or business. It also provides the academic background necessary to sit for the CFP® examination, the globally recognized professional certification in financial planning.

A minor in French requires a minimum of 18 hours, including 12 advanced hours. A minimum of 6 hours of advanced work must be completed at UNT.

Course Requirements:
FREN 1010, FREN 1020 (unless placement test shows competency)
FREN 2040, FREN 2050
FREN 3010, FREN 3020, FREN 3030, FREN 3040, FREN 3060, FREN 3070, FREN 3080
FREN 4010, FREN 4020, FREN 4030, FREN 4040, FREN 4050, FREN 4060, FREN 4070, FREN 4080

For more information, see the French section of the World Languages, Literatures and Cultures page in this catalog.

The General Business minor is designed for students who are not majoring in business but want to develop a general understanding of business principles. It provides students with a broad overview of essential business functions such as management, marketing, finance, and information technology. This minor can complement a wide range of non-business majors, enhancing career opportunities by adding a valuable business perspective.

Concentration name: General Geography, Urban and Regional Planning
description: A major in Geography helps students develop a global perspective on environmental and social issues, including climate change, natural hazards, land use, population change, cultural diversity, and urbanization. Students develop spatial thinking and problem-solving skills, and acquire proficiency with geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sensing technology to analyze geographic data. Graduates find career opportunities as urban and regional planners, environmental consultants, GIS analysts, demographers, cartographers, location analysts, and teachers. Our graduates also pursue graduate studies in geography and related fields.

Concentration name: Applied GIS, Atmospheric Science, Environmental Geography, Urban and Regional Planning
description: Geography is the study of earth as the home of humankind. Geographers investigate the spatial patterns and processes associated with human and natural phenomena. Geographers use various methods, including fieldwork, remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), global positioning systems (GPS), qualitative methods and statistical analysis. Geographers often address questions such as: Where are things located? Why are they located there? What are the consequences of their location? How are places formed? Geography offers a unique perspective for understanding complex global, regional and local issues, such as global warming, environmental degradation, natural hazards, economic development, political instability, urbanization and cultural conflict. Students in geography are prepared for a wide variety of careers in government, the private sector and education.

A minor in geography requires 18 semester hours, including at least 9 hours at the advanced level (3000- or 4000-level). A grade of C or better is required in all courses counted toward the minor. The minimum UNT GPA for minor courses is 2.0. This minor is designed to: Provide a basic understanding of geographic concepts and principles. Offer an opportunity to explore various aspects of the discipline, such as physical geography, human geography, geographic information science, and environmental studies. Enhance a student’s major by providing a broader perspective on spatial relationships and processes. Develop skills in spatial analysis and critical thinking. Courses completed to satisfy university core curriculum requirements may not be counted toward a minor. For more information about courses required for the minor, contact the Department of Geography and the Environment.

The Department of World Languages, Literatures and Cultures offers a Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in German. The German program offers students the opportunity to acquire proficiency in German and an in-depth understanding of German and German-speaking cultures within a global context. The German major helps students develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural communication, and cultural analysis as they prepare for a variety of careers or for further study.

The minor in German introduces students to the German language and to selected aspects of the literature and cultures of German-speaking countries. The minor requires a minimum of 18 semester hours in German with a GPA of at least 2.0 (C) in all courses counted toward the minor. A minimum of 6 semester hours must be taken at UNT.

The minor in Health and Wellness Studies promotes the development of knowledge and skills necessary to improve the health and well-being of individuals and communities. This interdisciplinary minor allows students to apply concepts of health promotion, disease prevention, and behavior change to a variety of professional and personal settings. Students will gain an understanding of health disparities, cultural competence, and ethical considerations in health and wellness. The minor prepares students for careers in public health, health education, corporate wellness, community health, and other related fields, or for further graduate study.

The Bachelor of Science in Health, Wellness and Community prepares students with the knowledge and skills to promote health and prevent disease for individuals, families and communities. The interdisciplinary curriculum addresses a wide range of health-related topics including nutrition, physical activity, mental health, substance use, chronic disease prevention and health disparities. The program emphasizes community health promotion strategies, health education, program planning and evaluation, and advocacy. Graduates are prepared for careers in public health agencies, non-profit organizations, corporate wellness programs and healthcare settings, or for graduate studies in public health, health administration, or related fields.

The Bachelor of Arts degree with a major in History provides students with an understanding of the past and the skills needed to interpret historical events. Through rigorous coursework, students learn to analyze primary and secondary sources, develop critical thinking abilities, and communicate effectively both orally and in writing. The program prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, government, museums, archives, and business. It also provides a solid foundation for graduate study in history or related disciplines.

A minor in history requires 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced. The department requires that 6 of the 18 hours must be in United States history; 3 hours must be in European history; and 3 hours must be in non-Western history. At least 9 hours must be taken at UNT. All courses counted toward the minor must be passed with a grade of C or better. Only one internship (HIST 4090) may count toward the minor.

The Home Furnishings Merchandising program prepares students for various positions in the residential and contract segments of the home furnishings industry. Students develop an understanding of home furnishings products and materials, product sourcing and distribution, merchandising, retail operations, sales, and entrepreneurial practices. The program offers a broad education in merchandising with a strong emphasis on business and marketing. This program includes a business minor and a required professional internship in the home furnishings industry. The department maintains close ties with the home furnishings industry, providing students with numerous opportunities for professional development and industry engagement.

The Bachelor of Science degree in hospitality management prepares students for leadership positions in the largest service industry in the world. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in business and management practices applicable to the hotel, restaurant, tourism, convention, club, casino and other segments of the hospitality industry.

The Department of Human Development and Family Science offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Human Development and Family Science designed to prepare students to work effectively with individuals and families in diverse settings. This program is for students interested in careers that focus on the development of individuals and families across the life span and within the context of diverse family structures and community systems. The curriculum offers opportunities to gain knowledge and skills in understanding individual and family dynamics, promoting healthy relationships, and addressing contemporary issues facing families. Students will also learn about child development, family theories, interventions, ethics, and research methods. The program integrates theory, research, and practice to equip students with the competencies needed for various professional roles, including family life education, social services, youth development, and early childhood education. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions in agencies, schools, hospitals, and non-profit organizations or for continued graduate studies in related fields. This academic program is accredited by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for meeting the high standards for the Provisional Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
Accreditation status: National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for meeting the high standards for the Provisional Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
Program name: Human Development and Family Science, BS

description: Human resource management involves the effective utilization of people to achieve organizational and individual goals. Students will acquire the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully meet the challenges facing today's human resource management professionals including strategic human resource management, human resource planning, staffing, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and HR information systems.

The Human Resource Management minor is designed to provide students with an understanding of various aspects of human resource management, including staffing, training and development, compensation, and legal issues. The minor requires a minimum of 18 semester hours with a minimum of 9 advanced hours from the courses listed below. All 18 semester hours for the minor must be completed at UNT.
Program name: Human Resource Management (Minor for non-business majors)

description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in Information Science provides an understanding of the concepts, systems, and tools for organizing, accessing, and using information. Students learn how to analyze, design, and manage information systems and services in a variety of organizational settings. Students also gain skills in information organization, information retrieval, information technologies, and user experience design. The degree provides opportunities for students to apply these skills in internships, research projects, and other experiential learning activities.
The Information Science, BS degree prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as data analysis, information management, knowledge management, library and information services, user experience design, and digital asset management. Graduates are prepared for positions in public and private sector organizations, including corporations, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and educational institutions. The degree also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in information science and related fields.

The Bachelor of Arts in Information Technology provides an interdisciplinary and applied course of study in the development, deployment, and management of information technology and information systems. The BA in IT prepares students to assume professional positions with a variety of technical and leadership responsibilities across a wide range of organizations.

Do you have a wide variety of academic interests and want to develop critical thinking skills across different subjects? The Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that allows students to combine three "focus areas" of study from different academic disciplines.

This degree plan is specifically designed to give you flexibility and independence to tailor your academic path based on your passions and career goals. You'll work closely with an academic advisor to select three 18-hour focus areas that align with your interests, career aspirations, and educational goals. The ability to integrate multiple fields of study is a valuable asset in today's dynamic job market.

This unique approach not only broadens your knowledge base but also enhances your problem-solving abilities, communication skills and critical thinking, preparing you for a wide range of career paths or graduate studies. Whether you are passionate about the arts, sciences, humanities, or a combination, the B.A. in Integrative Studies empowers you to build a degree that truly reflects your intellectual curiosity and professional ambitions.

The Bachelor of Science in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that gives students the opportunity to combine three academic areas of study into a single degree. This degree is designed for students who want to develop a broad knowledge base and skillset rather than specialize in one particular field. The unique combination of coursework provides students with a holistic view of several disciplines, thus giving graduates a wider range of career and/or graduate school options. This degree is especially well suited for students who want to build custom curricula in preparation for specific career fields not addressed by a single traditional major.

The Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies BA program offers a flexible curriculum focusing on critical thinking, research skills and writing while engaging in the theory and practice of art, design and visual culture. Students cultivate an understanding of art and design within broad historical, theoretical and social contexts, and gain a wide range of skills applicable to the professional world. The degree prepares students for a variety of careers in fields that utilize art and design in an interdisciplinary context, such as non-profit administration, museums and galleries, community engagement, arts advocacy, education, communications, entrepreneurship, and publishing. The degree also provides excellent preparation for graduate study in a range of fields, including art history, visual culture, museum education, and arts administration.
Program name: Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies, BA

description: Interior design is a creative, technical and analytical process used to develop interior environments that are healthy, safe, enjoyable and productive. The profession focuses on the building envelope and human interaction within that space. Interior designers have expertise in space planning, aesthetics, building codes, universal design, sustainable design, lighting, acoustics, materials and furnishings, and professional practice. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in residential, commercial and institutional design firms. The program culminates in a senior studio capstone experience and portfolio.
Accreditation status: The Interior Design program at the University of North Texas is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA), 206 Grandville Ave., Suite 350, Grand Rapids, MI, 49503.

Concentration name: Asian Studies Track, European Studies Track, Global Issues Track, Latin American Studies Track, Middle East & North African Studies Track
description: The international studies major is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the international community and global issues. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in government, non-profit organizations and business, and for graduate study in international relations, law, public administration, international business and related fields. The curriculum includes course work in the humanities, social sciences, business and foreign languages related to global issues, specific world regions and cross-cultural understanding. All international studies majors are required to demonstrate third-year proficiency in a foreign language.

The minor in Italian consists of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). Students must have completed ITAL 1010 and 1020 (or equivalent proficiency) prior to beginning the minor. The minor requires a minimum UNT GPA of 2.0.
A minor in Italian develops a student’s appreciation of Italian language and culture while complementing studies in a variety of fields such as art history, international studies, political science, history, literature, music, business and film.

The Bachelor of Arts in Japanese provides students with proficiency in Japanese language as well as a rich background in Japanese history, culture and literature. Students are also encouraged to develop competency in a second foreign language beyond the university’s foreign language requirement.

The Japanese minor provides students with the linguistic and cultural background to interact with Japanese-speaking communities and pursue various careers. A minor in Japanese requires a minimum of 18 hours, including 6 advanced hours. No more than 6 hours of Japanese may be counted toward both the minor and another major or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses counting toward the minor. Required courses: JAPN 2040 - Intermediate Japanese I (3 hours) JAPN 2050 - Intermediate Japanese II (3 hours) JAPN 3040 - Advanced Japanese I (3 hours) JAPN 3050 - Advanced Japanese II (3 hours) Plus 6 hours of Japanese at the 3000-4000 level. Up to 6 hours may be JAPN 3000.

The Minor in Jewish and Israel Studies requires 18 hours, 12 of which must be advanced (3000/4000) level, drawn from an approved list of courses. The minor is offered by the Department of History, and is housed within the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences.

Concentration name: Broadcast Journalism, Digital and Converged Journalism, News and Feature Journalism, Photojournalism
description: The Department of Journalism offers students instruction and professional preparation in the many varied aspects of journalism. Students are prepared to enter a wide variety of journalism careers including jobs in news, photojournalism, visual communication, editing, web design and development, data visualization, magazine, broadcast, and multimedia journalism. The curriculum emphasizes professional courses, internships and a strong liberal arts background with a major that encourages students to complete a minor in another field. The department also offers graduate degrees.

The Journalism minor gives students the opportunity to learn critical thinking, research, writing, reporting and multimedia storytelling skills for a variety of media professions. This minor is open to all students on campus, regardless of major. The minor offers flexibility for students to explore their interests in areas such as digital and broadcast journalism, strategic communications, or sports media. It also offers students an opportunity to learn current digital skills, including video, audio, social media and data journalism. By gaining knowledge and experience in journalism, students enhance their major while also improving their critical thinking, writing, and communication skills, which are vital for careers in any field.

The Department of Kinesiology offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Kinesiology. Students in this program are prepared for careers in health, fitness and wellness, sport management, and allied health professions. Emphasis is placed on human movement, health, fitness, and sport from a scientific, behavioral, and socio-cultural perspective. The undergraduate program in Kinesiology provides a broad background in exercise science, public health, and human movement studies and is designed to lead to entry-level positions in fitness, health, and sport professions, as well as prepare students for graduate study or professional schools. The Kinesiology undergraduate program offers three concentrations, allowing students to tailor their academic experience to their specific career interests.

The Latino/a and Mexican American Studies (LMAS) program offers a 18-hour undergraduate minor in interdisciplinary scholarship. Students completing the minor will develop a critically informed understanding of the histories, cultures, politics, and social experiences of Latino/a and Mexican American communities in the United States and transnationally. The minor introduces students to the major theoretical and methodological approaches to Latino/a and Mexican American Studies scholarship and provides opportunities to apply these to a variety of topics and issues. Through critical analysis of race, class, gender, and sexuality in historical and contemporary contexts, the LMAS minor provides students with the intellectual tools to engage with and contribute to social justice.

The Leadership Development minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to enhance the leadership competencies and capacity of students from all majors through a combination of coursework and experiential learning opportunities. The minor supports students in developing foundational leadership knowledge, skills, and abilities for a variety of contexts; understanding leadership from multiple perspectives, theories, and approaches; practicing leadership and working effectively in a team through experiential learning activities; identifying and clarifying personal values, ethics, and strengths relative to leadership; applying self-reflection and critical thinking to leadership practice; and communicating effectively and building relationships within and across diverse groups. Students will cultivate skills and experiences valuable in any profession or area of graduate study.

The minor in Legal Information Management provides students with a foundational understanding of the legal information profession, including the acquisition, organization, retrieval, and preservation of legal information resources. Students will develop skills in legal research, legal technology, and legal ethics, preparing them for careers in law libraries, legal departments, government agencies, and other organizations that require expertise in managing legal information. The minor is suitable for students pursuing a variety of majors, including those in political science, criminal justice, business, and information science. Students interested in the minor should contact the Department of Information Science for advising.

The minor in Legal Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a broad understanding of the legal system and its impact on society. The minor introduces students to the nature of law, legal reasoning, legal institutions, and the role of law in various social, economic, and political contexts. It also provides students with an opportunity to explore career paths in law and related fields. The minor complements a wide range of majors by providing valuable skills in critical thinking, analytical reasoning, research, and communication. These skills are essential for success in law school, graduate school, and various professional careers.

The LGBTQ Studies minor provides students with the critical skills and knowledge to understand lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer lives from an interdisciplinary perspective. This minor is designed to help students understand LGBTQ issues related to human sexuality, gender identity and expression, race/ethnicity, and social justice. The LGBTQ Studies minor provides the opportunity for students to complement their major with a focused program of study in LGBTQ history, culture, and experience. In addition, the minor prepares students for careers in LGBTQ advocacy and activism, public policy, social work, and education, among others. In a globalizing world, understanding issues of sexuality and gender is increasingly important. This minor is open to all students, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity.

The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in Logistics and Supply Chain Management prepares students for a wide range of career opportunities in the field of logistics and supply chain management. This field involves the planning, implementation and controlling of the efficient flow and storage of goods, services and related information from the point of origin to the point of consumption. It includes the management of activities such as inventory, warehousing, transportation, distribution, purchasing, supply management, global logistics, and supply chain strategy. Students will gain knowledge and skills in these key areas, preparing them for careers in various industries, including manufacturing, retail, transportation, consulting, and government. The program emphasizes analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, as well as an understanding of global supply chain issues and sustainability practices. Graduates will be equipped to manage and optimize complex supply chain operations, contributing to organizational efficiency and competitive advantage.
Program name: Logistics and Supply Chain Management, BBA

description: The Department of Management offers a major in Management leading to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) degree. This major provides a broad base of knowledge regarding the management of organizations. Students are prepared for careers in management, human resource management and entrepreneurship/small business management, as well as for further study at the graduate level. The curriculum helps students develop strong critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making and communication skills applicable to managing a business operation and its human resources.

The minor in management is designed to provide students with an overview of the role of managers in organizations. It includes courses in the basic principles of management, organizational behavior, human resource management and strategic management. This minor is open to all university students except those majoring in business fields. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor.

The Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing prepares students for a variety of careers across the marketing field. Marketing is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. Marketers play a key role in understanding customers, creating value, communicating value, and delivering value. The marketing major provides students with the fundamental knowledge needed to succeed in areas such as professional selling and sales management, digital marketing, marketing analytics, supply chain management, retail management, brand management, marketing research and advertising.

The marketing minor is designed to provide non-business majors with an opportunity to acquire fundamental marketing knowledge and skills. Students completing the marketing minor will be prepared to integrate marketing concepts into their primary field of study. The minor provides an excellent supplement for students in a variety of fields such as communication, hospitality management, merchandising, journalism, music, visual arts and general studies, to name a few. The minor will help students increase their marketability in the workplace.

Materials science and engineering is an interdisciplinary field that deals with the discovery and design of new materials. Materials are at the heart of all engineering disciplines; they determine product characteristics and functionality across all aspects of our lives. Materials science and engineering majors learn about the relationships between properties, structure, processing and performance of engineering materials. This knowledge prepares students for successful careers in academia, industry and national laboratories. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Materials Science and Engineering, a Master of Science (MS) in Materials Science and Engineering, and a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering. The department also offers a minor in materials science and engineering. The BS in Materials Science and Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in Mathematics is an excellent choice for students who want a broad liberal arts education but who also want to obtain a solid grounding in mathematics. Many students pursue this degree in combination with another major in a field such as economics, computer science, business or the sciences. This degree also provides students with the background needed for teaching mathematics in grades 7-12 (with proper certification), and it can be used as preparation for graduate study in mathematics or in a related field. The BA in Mathematics requires courses in mathematics, statistics and computer science, as well as a foreign language.

Concentration name: Secondary Teacher Certification, Standard, Computer Science concentration
description: Mathematics is the basis for all scientific and technological advancements, which makes it a valuable degree in many fields. The UNT Department of Mathematics provides a fundamental grounding in mathematical theory, as well as opportunities to apply mathematics to real-world problems. Our bachelor's degree program is the study of quantity, structure, space, and change. Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as engineering, finance, computer science, education and the sciences. The Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Mathematics is offered with two tracks, Secondary Teacher Certification and Standard. In addition, there is a Computer Science concentration. Students are provided with a rigorous mathematical training that prepares them for graduate study or careers as teachers, actuaries, financial analysts or data scientists.

Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest and oldest engineering disciplines and is concerned with the design, development, manufacture, operation, maintenance and control of various machines, processes and systems. Mechanical engineers apply scientific principles to solve real-world problems. The energy engineering component focuses on energy systems analysis, design and applications, including both conventional and renewable energy technologies. Mechanical and Energy Engineering (MEE) graduates are highly sought after by employers due to their strong analytical and problem-solving skills as well as their ability to adapt to changes and new challenges. Many MEE graduates work for consulting firms, research and development companies, utilities, and various manufacturing industries. With a strong background in analytical skills, many graduates also pursue advanced degrees in engineering and science, business, law and medicine. Our graduates are equipped with a strong fundamental understanding of design, mechanical systems, thermal systems, materials and manufacturing processes. They apply engineering principles to the solution of problems involving energy conversion systems, power plants, heating, ventilating and air conditioning, robotics, manufacturing, instrumentation and control, transportation systems, medical equipment, biomechanical systems, micro-electro-mechanical systems, product design and development, and various other industries.
Accreditation status: The program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
