description: Mechanical engineering technology is a practice-oriented engineering discipline that focuses on the application of specific technologies. Students gain knowledge and skills in material science, manufacturing processes, computer-aided design, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, machine design and instrumentation and control. These skills are critical in a wide range of industries including aerospace, biomedical, energy production, manufacturing, robotics and automation. Students are prepared for careers in the private sector and government as applied mechanical engineers. Graduates contribute to product design, development, quality assurance, manufacturing processes, maintenance and sales.
Accreditation status: The Mechanical Engineering Technology, BS program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Media Arts provides students with a broad education in the history, theory and aesthetics of media arts, along with production experience in film, television, audio, video and interactive media. This program serves students who wish to pursue careers in the media industries and/or graduate study.

A minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of the cultures and civilizations of the medieval and Renaissance periods. The minor introduces students to the major literary, artistic, philosophical, religious, social and political developments of the periods, as well as the important figures who helped shape them. The minor is flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests. It encourages students to work closely with faculty in a variety of departments, including Art History, English, History, Languages, Literatures and Cultures, Music and Philosophy. Because the minor requires students to consider texts and works of art from multiple perspectives, it promotes critical thinking skills that are highly valued in any profession.

The Department of Merchandising and Digital Retailing in the College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism offers the Bachelor of Science (BS) with a major in Merchandising. The curriculum provides the student with knowledge of the flow of goods and services from producer to consumer and with an understanding of global and socio-economic influences on merchandise movement. The areas of emphasis are buying, product development, retail management, global retailing, visual merchandising, merchandise planning and allocation, fashion promotion and analysis, and fashion history. Internships provide students with professional work experience and networking opportunities. Graduates pursue careers in the merchandising field in retailing, apparel, home furnishings, accessories and related industries.

The Minor in Merchandising prepares students for successful careers in merchandising and related fields such as product development, buying, planning, allocation, visual merchandising and retail management. The curriculum provides a foundation in merchandising theories and practices. Students are exposed to both domestic and global industry operations within various segments of the retail industry. This minor is open to all students on campus; however, students must consult with a Merchandising academic advisor to assure prerequisites are completed.

The Military Science program (Army ROTC) provides leadership training through classroom instruction and practical exercises. Students learn to lead, coach and motivate groups of people to accomplish challenging missions in various environments. The program gives students the skills and tools they need to succeed in any career field, whether they pursue a career in the military or in the private sector. The Minor in Military Science is designed for students who are already participating in Army ROTC and wish to earn academic credit for their ROTC studies. The minor helps broaden students’ educational experience while preparing them for leadership challenges in a complex world. The curriculum covers foundational military knowledge, leadership principles, ethics, and critical thinking. The minor is suitable for students from any academic major and offers a pathway for those considering a career as an officer in the U.S. Army. Students in the Military Science program participate in rigorous training and development activities, including physical fitness, field training exercises, and leadership labs. They develop problem-solving skills, decision-making abilities, and a strong sense of discipline and teamwork. The program also offers opportunities for scholarships and stipends.

The Bachelor of Arts in Music degree allows students to combine the serious study of music with a broad liberal arts education. It is designed for students who desire a comprehensive education emphasizing music history, theory, and performance, along with the opportunity to pursue other academic areas in a minor or a concentration. The BA degree is available to students whose goals include preparation for graduate study in musicology or ethnomusicology, preparation for careers in music business or arts administration, and for those who wish to pursue a dual major.

The Bachelor of Music (BM) in music education prepares students for careers as music teachers in public and private schools. Students are prepared to seek all-level certification to teach instrumental, choral and general music.

The Bachelor of Music in Composition provides students with a strong foundation in compositional techniques, theory, history, and musicianship. Students will develop their unique compositional voice and create original works across various genres and instrumentation. The program prepares graduates for further graduate study in composition or careers as composers, educators, or other music professionals.

The Bachelor of Music in music: general is a program intended for students whose musical interests are diverse and do not fall into the more specific and specialized BM programs offered by the College of Music. This degree provides a solid foundation in music while offering flexibility for students to tailor electives and coursework according to their individual interests. Students who pursue this degree may be interested in a variety of musical pursuits, including entrepreneurship, arts administration, or other multidisciplinary careers.

The Bachelor of Music (BM) in Jazz Studies requires 120 hours and provides a rigorous, comprehensive study of jazz performance, history, theory, and improvisation. Students develop skills in improvisation, composition, arranging, and musicianship, preparing them for careers as professional jazz musicians, educators, or composers. The curriculum emphasizes both practical experience through ensembles and theoretical knowledge through coursework. Students may choose one of three concentrations: Jazz Performance, Jazz Composition, or Jazz Entrepreneurship.

The Bachelor of Music in performance is for students who intend to pursue careers as performers, teachers of performance, or further study in performance at the graduate level. Students specialize in a specific instrument (brass, guitar, keyboard, percussion, strings, voice, woodwinds) or conducting, jazz studies (instrumental or vocal), or vocal or instrumental music education. In addition to music courses, students take courses in the university core curriculum.
Accreditation status: UNT’s music program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: New Media Art is an interdisciplinary program that emphasizes experimentation and innovation within contemporary art practices. Areas of focus include electronic sculpture and installation, video art, interactivity, sound art, performance, AR/VR, animation, computer programming, web-based art, digital fabrication, and expanded cinema. Students engage in critical discourse about the social, political, and cultural implications of new technologies and media. The program is designed to develop students’ artistic vision and technical proficiency through hands-on studio experiences and theoretical explorations.

The Nonprofit Leadership Studies minor provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills to lead and manage nonprofit organizations. The curriculum provides an overview of the nonprofit sector and focuses on developing competencies in areas such as fundraising, grant writing, volunteer management, program evaluation, and board governance. Students will gain practical experience through internships and community engagement opportunities, preparing them for careers in nonprofit management, social entrepreneurship, and public service.

The minor in operations and supply chain management is designed for non-business majors interested in understanding how organizations manage their operations, supply chains, and projects. Students completing the minor will develop skills in the areas of supply chain analytics, process improvement, logistics and inventory management, global sourcing, and project management. The minor will provide a pathway for students to develop a specialization that complements their major and enhances their employability in various industries. The minor requires a minimum of 18 hours, with at least 9 hours at the 3000-4000 level and 9 hours in residence. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required on all courses counted toward the minor. The minor is only available to non-business majors.
Program name: Operations and Supply Chain Management (Minor for non-business majors)

description: The Department of Management offers a minor in Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management. This minor provides students with knowledge and skills relevant to the behavior of individuals and groups within organizations, and to the management of human resources.
Program name: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management (Minor)

description: The Bachelor of Science degree in organizational leadership prepares students to lead and motivate others in a variety of settings. Students learn about leadership strategies and practices, human resource management, decision-making, and organizational development and change. The program develops the skills required to be an effective leader in today’s dynamic business environment. This degree is designed for students who are looking to complete their undergraduate degree and either enter the workforce or continue on to graduate school.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Painting and Drawing is designed to prepare students for careers as professional artists and for graduate studies in painting and drawing. This degree plan offers an intensive studio experience complemented by art history and academic courses.
Accreditation status: The Department of Visual Arts and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description: The Peace Studies minor at the University of North Texas brings together a range of courses concerned with the causes of peace and violence, the development of peaceful resolutions to conflicts, and the role of social justice in fostering peace. In this minor, students will integrate approaches to the study of peace from a range of different disciplines, including philosophy, political science, sociology, history, and communication. The minor includes courses that deal with theoretical approaches to peace and courses that demonstrate applied skills needed for peace-building work. The minor helps prepare students for a variety of careers in both governmental and non-governmental organizations at local, national and international levels. Students with a minor in Peace Studies will also be better prepared for graduate study in fields such as international relations, human rights, law, public policy, and social work.

The UNT Philosophy Department offers a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in philosophy, a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree with a major in philosophy and a concentration in religious studies, a minor in philosophy, a minor in religious studies, and a Master of Arts (MA) degree in philosophy. The department is a welcoming and inclusive intellectual home for a diverse community of faculty and students. Philosophy is an ancient, yet continually developing discipline that equips students with skills central to success in all areas of life, work and citizenship. Students in the program develop excellent critical thinking, analytical, communication and research skills. Philosophy majors have high rates of success on graduate school entrance exams and are attractive candidates for a variety of careers in law, public service, business, education, non-profits, journalism and medicine. Many philosophy majors pursue graduate study in philosophy or other academic fields. The department also hosts a number of events throughout the year, including talks by visiting scholars, a colloquium series, and the UNT Undergraduate Philosophy Conference.

A minor in philosophy consists of 18 hours in philosophy, at least 9 of which must be advanced (3000- or 4000-level). No more than 3 hours of credit for a directed study course (PHIL 4900) may count toward the minor. The student must earn a grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor. For information regarding advising, contact the Department of Philosophy and Religion. A grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor.

The photography program focuses on contemporary practices that explore both traditional and new media. As an undergraduate, you’ll be exposed to fundamental and advanced technical and aesthetic practices necessary to build a broad understanding of the medium. We offer studio courses, lectures, digital photography courses, and an extensive darkroom and studio facility. Throughout the program, you’ll take courses in a variety of areas including black and white, color, digital, alternative processes and studio lighting. You’ll be encouraged to expand your understanding of the medium, both in practice and in theory, through critical dialogue with faculty and peers, and through individual research.

The Bachelor of Arts in Physics provides students with a broad background in physics and mathematics. Students graduating with a BA in Physics find success in various fields, including science, medicine, computer science, law, and business. The BA in Physics can also be used to pursue graduate studies in physics or related fields. The BA in Physics degree is particularly well-suited for students who plan to combine a physics education with another major, a minor, or teacher certification requirements in a four-year program.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in physics is a strong major for students interested in a wide variety of careers, including positions in industry, government and education, or for students who wish to pursue graduate study in physics, astronomy or related fields. Students are provided with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of classical and modern physics, and in the mathematical and experimental techniques used in physics. Students who major in physics must complete either the Bachelor of Science with a concentration in Astrophysics or the Bachelor of Science with a concentration in Physics, General.

A minor in physics is designed for students seeking to obtain a basic understanding of physics concepts and principles. The minor is suitable for a wide variety of students whose majors are outside the physics field but who need or desire a foundational background in physics.

Concentration name: American Politics; Comparative Politics; International Relations; Public Policy; Political Theory
description: The Bachelor of Arts in political science offers a comprehensive study of American government, political theory, international relations and comparative politics. Students learn about the fundamental principles underlying political systems and behavior, the workings of governments and international organizations, and the dynamics of political change. The program provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers in government, law, business, journalism and teaching, or for graduate study.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Printmaking provides an opportunity for students to study the many processes of printmaking. The program provides the students with technical skills, conceptual development, and an understanding of the historical, critical and aesthetic issues of print media. Studio experience is supplemented by a broad range of liberal arts courses designed to expand students’ knowledge of the humanities and sciences. The program prepares students for graduate study and careers as professional artists, designers, illustrators, educators, or other art-related fields.

Professional and technical communicators are experts at making complex information understandable for diverse audiences and purposes. They translate complex, specialized information into effective messages for a variety of media. These skills are highly valued and highly marketable in a wide range of fields, including health care, engineering, information technology, business, government, education, and many others. Our graduates have found jobs in many roles including technical writers, editors, user experience researchers, content strategists, proposal writers, grant writers, web content developers, and more. A degree in Professional and Technical Communication prepares students to critically analyze and adapt to new technologies; organize information for clarity and effect; conduct user-centered research; design effective print and online documents; and manage projects.

The Professional Selling minor is designed for non-business majors interested in developing skills in sales and sales management. The coursework provides a strong foundation in professional selling, sales management, and organizational leadership, preparing students for successful careers in various industries requiring strong interpersonal, communication and negotiation skills. The minor also includes an internship requirement, providing students with valuable real-world experience.

The Department of Psychology offers the Bachelor of Arts (BA) in psychology and the Bachelor of Science (BS) in psychology. The BA provides a broad foundation in psychology, preparing students for a variety of careers and for graduate study in fields such as social work, counseling, business, or law.

This program is designed for students who wish to pursue a Bachelor of Science (BS) in psychology. The BS degree emphasizes psychological research and analysis and is intended for students who plan to continue their education in graduate school, especially in research-oriented fields, or who plan to enter careers for which a strong background in scientific psychology is appropriate. Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The goal of the psychology curriculum is to provide students with an understanding of psychological principles and research methods. A major in psychology provides a strong liberal arts background for students planning careers in a wide range of fields or for those planning to pursue graduate education.

The Bachelor of Science in Public Administration program prepares students for careers in federal, state and local government agencies and nonprofit organizations. Students gain an understanding of the structure and function of government, policy processes, and administrative practices. The curriculum emphasizes analytical skills, ethical decision-making, and effective communication, essential for addressing complex societal challenges. The program also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in public administration, public policy, and law.

The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Public Relations program provides students with the theoretical background and practical skills needed for successful careers in public relations. Students learn to research, plan, implement, and evaluate public relations programs through courses in public relations writing, research, campaigns, and ethics. This curriculum prepares students for a variety of roles in corporate, non-profit, government, and agency settings. The program also emphasizes the importance of strategic communication, media relations, crisis management, and digital communication, equipping graduates with a comprehensive skillset for the evolving public relations landscape. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions such as public relations specialist, media relations coordinator, social media manager, and communications assistant, and are well-positioned for career advancement within the field.

A minor in Public Relations provides students with a foundational understanding of the theories, principles and practices of contemporary public relations. Students learn about the role of public relations in society, ethical considerations, strategic communication planning, media relations, crisis communication and digital public relations. The curriculum also emphasizes the development of practical skills, such as writing for various public relations contexts, conducting research and executing communication campaigns. A public relations minor can complement a wide range of majors, enhancing students’ career prospects in fields such as marketing, journalism, business, political science, non-profit management and more.

The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in Real Estate provides an understanding of both the theoretical and practical aspects of real estate markets and finance. The degree helps students develop skills in areas such as real estate valuation, investment, financing, law, and development. The curriculum also prepares students for careers in real estate brokerage, appraisal, property management, and other related fields. Real estate courses are taught by faculty with doctoral degrees from major universities and extensive industry experience. The real estate program at UNT provides excellent opportunities for students to interact with industry professionals through mentoring programs, internships, and various student organizations. The program also features opportunities to participate in national competitions, conferences, and career fairs. The Real Estate program offers a curriculum that meets the educational requirements for the Texas Real Estate Salesperson License. Students completing the Real Estate program will have completed the 180 clock-hours of coursework required by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) to apply for the salesperson license. Students interested in obtaining the license must apply to TREC directly and meet all other TREC requirements for licensure. For more information, please visit www.trec.texas.gov.

The minor in Real Estate is designed to provide students with the opportunity to gain a basic understanding of real estate markets, transactions, investments, development and finance. The minor consists of 18 hours, nine of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level).

The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Recreation, Event and Sport Management provides students with knowledge, skills and abilities required for successful careers in recreation, event and sport management. The program’s curriculum provides students with a strong theoretical understanding of management principles, while concurrently providing students with the practical skills and hands-on experiences necessary to become leaders in the field.

Students will learn to plan, organize, lead and evaluate recreation, event and sport management programs and services. Students will also gain expertise in areas such as facility management, marketing and promotion, budgeting, legal aspects, risk management, and human resource management related to the recreation, event and sport industry. The program prepares students for careers in diverse settings including municipal recreation departments, non-profit organizations, commercial recreation businesses, event planning companies, sport organizations, and colleges/universities. Graduates are equipped to pursue professional certifications and advanced degrees in related fields.
Program name: Recreation, Event and Sport Management, BS

description: The bachelor of science (BS) in rehabilitation studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in rehabilitation or related fields, including entry-level positions in state and federal rehabilitation agencies, community-based rehabilitation programs, substance abuse programs, psychiatric rehabilitation programs, vocational rehabilitation, disability services, supported employment, and other human services organizations. The program also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in rehabilitation counseling, addiction counseling, social work, special education, and other human service professions. Students acquire the knowledge, values, and skills necessary to work effectively with persons with disabilities and other disadvantaged populations to improve their quality of life. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including rehabilitation principles, counseling theories and techniques, case management, vocational assessment, job placement, psychosocial aspects of disability, ethics, and cultural diversity. Students complete a supervised practicum and internship experience in a rehabilitation setting to gain practical skills.

The interdisciplinary religious studies minor brings together faculty from departments across the university to provide students with a broad understanding of the forms, functions and history of religion. The minor prepares students for graduate study in religion, seminary, and for a variety of professions in which knowledge of religion is critical, including teaching, law, social work, journalism, public service and the arts. The minor helps students develop critical thinking and communication skills and an understanding of diverse peoples and cultures.

The Retailing minor is designed for students outside the G. Brint Ryan College of Business who want to gain expertise in retailing operations and strategies. The minor complements a variety of majors including fashion design, merchandising, communication studies, hospitality management, journalism, marketing (non-business major), and visual arts. Students completing the minor will have an understanding of the retail industry including store operations, buying, supply chain issues and marketing.

Students in risk management and insurance learn to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks associated with business operations. They gain an understanding of how insurance works, including different types of coverage, policies, and regulations. They also learn about risk assessment, loss control, and claims management. Graduates with a BBA in risk management and insurance are prepared for careers in various sectors, including insurance companies, brokerage firms, corporate risk management departments, and regulatory agencies. Common job titles include insurance underwriter, claims adjuster, risk analyst, and employee benefits specialist. The curriculum covers topics such as property and liability insurance, life and health insurance, employee benefits, and enterprise risk management. Students develop analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for success in this dynamic field.
Accreditation status: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

Program name: Risk Management and Insurance (Minor for non-business majors)

description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in sculpture challenges students to explore sculpture as a creative discipline through traditional and contemporary processes, while developing critical thinking skills and an understanding of historical and cultural perspectives. Students have access to a variety of resources, including a foundry, woodshop, fabrication lab, and digital fabrication equipment, and the program encourages an interdisciplinary approach to art-making, providing students with opportunities to engage in collaborations across disciplines within the College of Visual Arts and Design and the larger university. With a focus on professional development, the BFA in sculpture prepares students for careers as artists, educators, and cultural leaders, and for continued study at the graduate level.

The Bachelor of Arts with a major in social science is an interdisciplinary degree program that is designed to help students understand the complexity of social systems and human behavior. It is for students interested in a broad-based education in the social sciences rather than a specific major in one discipline, providing flexibility for those who wish to pursue a course of study that draws from multiple social science areas (anthropology, criminal justice, economics, geography, history, political science, psychology, sociology). The degree is particularly well suited for students preparing for careers in teaching, government service, social justice, or other fields requiring a broad understanding of society and human behavior. The program requires a combination of 18 hours in two selected areas of concentration from the social sciences listed above, along with a specified number of additional hours from the remaining social science areas, for a total of 42 hours. This provides students with an opportunity to gain deeper knowledge in two areas while also maintaining a broad understanding of the social sciences as a whole.

The Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program prepares students for beginning generalist social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and organizations. Students in the program develop a strong foundation in social work values, ethics, and principles, and learn to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to address social justice issues. The curriculum emphasizes a holistic approach to understanding human behavior in the social environment, and promotes cultural competence and diversity. Graduates are prepared for a variety of entry-level social work positions in settings such as child welfare, mental health, healthcare, schools, and community organizations. The BSW program also provides a strong foundation for students interested in pursuing graduate studies in social work (MSW) or related fields.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).

description: The Sociology program provides students with a strong foundation in sociological theory and research methods, preparing them for a variety of careers and graduate studies. Sociology is the scientific study of human social life, groups and societies. It is a dazzling and compelling enterprise, having as its subject matter our own behavior as social beings. The scope of sociology is extremely wide, ranging from the analysis of passing encounters between individuals on the street to the investigation of global social processes. The program will enable students to think critically about society, social problems, and social inequality. The program encourages students to develop their own analytical and research interests through coursework and faculty mentorship. Students graduating with a BA in Sociology are prepared for positions in social services, public policy, market research, human resources, and numerous other fields. Graduates are also well-prepared for graduate study in sociology, law, social work, public administration, business and other fields.

The Bachelor of Science degree with a major in sociology is intended for students who wish to pursue graduate work in the discipline or who plan to enter law school or pursue a career that requires strong research and analytical skills in human behavior. It stresses methodological competence through courses in statistics and research methods. At the graduate level, the department offers graduate courses in sociological theory, research methods, and the substantive fields of sociology, as well as opportunities for research on topics of specific interest to students.

The minor in sociology provides students an opportunity to learn the core concepts and methods of sociological inquiry and to apply that knowledge to the analysis of social issues. A sociology minor provides students with a strong foundation in social analysis for careers in criminal justice, social work, human resources, law, public policy, community development and urban planning, and education. The minor also helps students develop critical thinking, analytic and research skills that are highly valued in any field. Students often combine the sociology minor with a major in business, criminal justice, education, public administration, political science, psychology, or social work.

Concentration name: ceramics, communication design, drawing and painting, fashion design, fiber arts, metalsmithing and jewelry, new media art, photography, printmaking, or sculpture
description: The Bachelor of Arts in Studio Art degree is a liberal arts degree. It provides students with a broad background in general studies, art history and theory, and studio art. The BA degree can be completed with a specialization in one of the studio art areas offered in the Department of Studio Art. Students pursuing a BA in Studio Art may earn teacher certification by combining their degree with an approved teacher certification program within the College of Visual Arts and Design.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Studio Art requires 120 hours, of which at least 42 must be advanced. It is a professional degree that provides in-depth study in one of the following emphasis areas: Ceramics, Fibers, Metalsmithing & Jewelry, New Media, Painting & Drawing, Photography, Printmaking or Sculpture. The program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career as a practicing artist, or for those who plan to pursue graduate study in the visual arts. The curriculum includes a strong foundation in visual art principles, art history, and critical thinking. Students develop a comprehensive portfolio of work in their chosen emphasis area, culminating in a senior exhibition. Studio Art majors are eligible to participate in various departmental opportunities, including student organizations, internships, and study abroad programs. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in the arts, including professional artists, gallery assistants, art educators, museum technicians, and art consultants, or for continued study in MFA programs.

The College of Education prepares professional educators in a variety of licensure areas. The Teacher Education program offers certification in multiple subject areas and grade levels. Students admitted to a teacher education program must follow the current degree and certification requirements in effect at the time of admission to the program. All students are advised to seek advising from the College of Education advising office. Additionally, students are advised to obtain a current list of all certification requirements from the UNT Educator Certification Office for updates to the state teacher certification requirements.

The minor in technical communication gives students in other disciplines an opportunity to develop expertise in the theory and practice of technical communication. Through study and practice in technical communication strategies, students will learn to communicate complex information to a variety of audiences, in a variety of contexts, and using a variety of media. These skills will prepare students to communicate effectively in the workplace and to understand the role of communication in their chosen fields. Students will develop skills in the following areas: audience analysis, information design, usability, editing, document production, and project management. Students learn to use these skills to create effective print and electronic documents, including proposals, reports, manuals, presentations, and websites. The minor supports careers in industry, government, education, and publishing.

Concentration name: Acting, Design and Technology, Directing, Playwriting, Theatre Studies (Liberal Arts)
description: The Bachelor of Arts in Theatre provides a broad-based, liberal arts degree designed to provide students with a background in theatrical history, theory, literature and dramatic criticism, as well as a basis in the practice of theatre. Students in the BA in Theatre program will select an advising track in one of the following areas: Acting, Design and Technology, Directing, Playwriting or Theatre Studies (Liberal Arts).
A minor in theatre is offered through the Department of Dance and Theatre. A minor in theatre consists of 18 semester hours, including at least 6 advanced hours, as follows:

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre with a major in Performance trains students for careers in acting and/or musical theatre performance. This intensive and highly selective program is designed to develop the actor’s craft through studio and classroom work, with additional training in voice, movement, dance, and music. Performance majors also gain hands-on experience through the department’s extensive production season.

The minor in urban policy and planning provides students with a foundational understanding of the theories, policies, and practices related to urban development, governance, and planning. Students will learn about the challenges and opportunities facing urban areas, including issues of sustainability, social equity, economic development, and environmental justice. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary approaches to address complex urban issues. Graduates with this minor will be prepared for careers in government, non-profit organizations, and private consulting firms, or for further graduate study in urban planning, public policy, or related fields.

This degree is designed to prepare students for careers or graduate study in studio and art history, art education, visual art studies and art administration areas. The curriculum allows students to explore traditional studio disciplines, digital fabrication and computational art practices, and art history/theory while establishing a foundation of critical thinking and creative problem solving. Students will gain knowledge of current practices, technologies, theories and histories of art, and will develop their own creative and intellectual voices. Emphasis is placed on developing a strong portfolio of creative work that represents both disciplinary expertise and innovative research.

The Women's and Gender Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a critical awareness of the history, theories, and issues surrounding women, gender and sexuality. Students will gain an understanding of gender as a social and cultural construct and how it intersects with other social categories, such as race, ethnicity, class, ability, age and sexual identity. Students will explore how these categories shape individual identities, social institutions, cultural practices and political processes. The minor is suitable for all students, especially those planning to enter professions in which an understanding of gender, women and sexuality is important, such as law, medicine, social work, business, communications, education and human services.

Concentration name: Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Russian, Spanish
description: Students majoring in World Languages, Literatures and Cultures may pursue a primary specialization in Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Russian or Spanish. The World Languages, Literatures and Cultures major provides an excellent background for graduate study in the humanities and social sciences. It also prepares students for careers in teaching, government, journalism, international business, and other fields demanding advanced linguistic, analytical and cross-cultural skills.
Program name: World Languages, Literatures and Cultures, BA
